messages.content: i want to make a picture for my sister, but i keep thinking about whether everyone else will like it.
what does your sister like to look at or draw herself? that could help you choose something that is for her, rather than trying to please everyone.
she likes pictures of an old house. my brother likes animals and says a house will be too quiet.
your brother can like animals while your sister likes a picture of a house. the picture is for her, so what she enjoys is useful information.
say that in a shorter way.
your brother likes animals. your sister likes a picture of a house. the picture is for your sister, so her choice can help you choose what to draw.
i want to draw the house we lived in when we were little.
that could give the picture a meaning for both of you. you could draw the parts you remember clearly, such as a door or a tree.
give me just the things i could draw.
you could draw the old house, with the door and tree you remember clearly.
what if i cannot remember the color of the door?
you could ask your sister, look for a photo, or leave the color out. you do not have to say you remember something you do not.
can you tell me what this is?
i need a little more information about what you mean by this. can you tell me about the object or give me its name?
i can see it, so why can you not just answer?
you can see the object where you are. i do not see it from your words alone. if you tell me what it looks like, i can try to help.
give me a more simple explanation.
you can see the object. i need you to tell me about it before i can help with a question about it.
it is a small thing with a circle shape, and it is on my desk.
that could be many things. what is it made of, and what do you use it for?
i use it to keep a place in a book.
you use it to show where you stopped reading. from that use, it sounds like an object for keeping your place in the book. i still do not know what you call that specific object.
is that a better answer than making up a name?
yes. it keeps the difference between the use you gave and the name we do not know.
i want soup for lunch, but my father says he is already making rice. should i tell him to stop?
you could first ask how far he has got and whether changing the meal would make more work. your wish for soup does not mean the rice must be stopped without talking about it.
use only our words. he has not started cooking yet, but he has put the pan and rice ready.
then you can still talk about the choice before cooking starts. you could ask whether soup would work today or whether he wants to keep the rice plan.
just write a question for him.
would soup work for lunch today, or would you rather make rice?
he said the rice is for dinner, not lunch. i had understood the plan wrong.
then soup for lunch and rice for dinner can both be part of the day. they are different meals.
say that more simply.
you can have soup for lunch and rice for dinner. one is for lunch, and the other is for dinner.
what should i say to him now?
i did not understand your plan before. thank you for telling me. i would like soup for lunch if that works for you.
i want to go to the library after lunch, but i do not know whether it will be open. can i write that i am sure i will get a book today?
not from the information you gave. you can plan to visit, but getting a book needs the library to be open and a book you want to be there.
use only simple words. give me a sentence with if.
if the library is open after lunch and has a book i want, i will get a book today.
what if it is open but the book i want is not there?
then the library is open, but the book you want is not there. you might choose another book or wait.
what choices would i have then?
the library is open, but you still cannot get that specific book if it is not there. you could choose another book or come back another day.
i only want one book, and i do not want to choose another.
then your plan can stay simple: check whether that book is there, and wait for another day if it is not.
can you say there would be no reason for the visit if the book is not there?
not unless that is how you feel about it. you could still learn whether the book is there, even if you do not take one home.
i have a book that my mother gave me and a book that my uncle gave me. the first is on the shelf. the other is on the table. where is the book that my uncle gave me?
on the table.
why did you not answer on the shelf?
because the words that my uncle gave me tell us which book you mean. that is the other book, not the first one from your mother.
now my mother moves the book on the table to the desk. did she give me that book?
no. moving the book now does not change who gave it to you. the book your uncle gave you is now on the desk.
what if i just ask where is her book?
that could mean more than one thing. you might mean the book your mother gave you, or a book she still has as her own. i would ask which book you mean.
make that answer more simple.
i would ask which book you mean. her book could mean the book your mother gave you or a book that is still hers.
ask me that question and nothing else.
which book do you mean?
the one my uncle gave me. answer with just the place.
on the desk.
write a short story using i about a day spent with a grandfather. start in the morning and end in the evening.

i went to see my grandfather after breakfast. he was sitting by the window with a book, and he asked whether i wanted to walk with him. we went slowly along the road and looked at the garden near his house. at lunch, we made soup and talked about the places where he had lived. in the afternoon, he showed me an old photo and told me about the people in it. before i left, i wrote down who the people were so i could remember them. as evening came, i put the paper in my book and said goodbye. i went home thinking about our quiet day together.
give me only the part about how i tried to remember the people.
before i left, i wrote down who the people were so i could remember them.
who is i in the story?
i is the person telling the story about visiting their grandfather.
did the story say the grandfather went home at the end?
no. the person telling the story went home. the grandfather was at his own house during the visit.
what was the paper for?
it was to help the person remember who was in the old photo.
make the last answer shorter.
it helped them remember the people in the photo.
my friend said we should walk along the road by the school to reach the park. that road is closed today. does that mean we cannot visit the park at all?
not always. one road may be closed while another way is still open. do you know another road that goes to the park?
use only the words we have. there is another road by the library, but it is a longer walk.
then the park may still be possible to visit by the library road. you would need to think about whether you have enough time for the longer walk.
we have the whole afternoon, so there is time for a longer walk.
from that information, the longer walk could work. you can change the way you go without changing the place you want to visit.
give me one short plan.
walk to the park by the library road, if that road is open and works for you.
do you know that the other road is open?
no. you said there is another road, but you did not say you checked whether it is open today. i should keep that part as something to check.
what should i tell my friend before leaving?
the school road is closed. we could use the library road, but we should check that it is open first.
i found a note that says i left your book by the window. it does not have a name. can you tell me who wrote it?
no. that note gives you information about the book, but it does not tell me which person wrote the words.
my sister usually writes a note like that. should i say it must be her?
you can say she is one possible person to ask. usually writing that kind of note does not mean she wrote this one.
give me a shorter answer.
your sister may have written it, but the note alone does not tell us who wrote it. you could ask her.
give me just the question for her.
did you leave the note about my book by the window?
what if she says she moved the book but did not write anything?
then moving the book and writing the note are two different parts of what happened. you would know she moved it, but still not know who wrote the note.
write only the information i would know after that.
your sister moved the book. she did not write the note, from what she told you.
my brother said he would help me with my drawing today. now he says he needs to finish his work first. does that mean he will never help?
not from those words. he said he needs to finish something first. you still need to know whether there will be time for helping you after that.
i am worried because i have to take the drawing to school tomorrow morning.
then tell him about that time. it is useful information for choosing whether his later help will still work for you.
write one question that keeps both our needs in it.
will you have time to help with my drawing after your work, before i need to take it to school tomorrow?
he says he cannot know yet. should i just leave the drawing without doing anything more?
you could work on the parts you can do yourself and choose another way to get help if needed. waiting without doing anything might leave you with less time.
give me a short plan for what i can do now.
keep working on the parts you can do now. if he has time later, he can help with the parts that are still hard.
what would you ask me before giving more specific help?
i would ask which part of the drawing you need help with.
my friend asked me to teach her a song. i know the words, but i do not know how to explain everything at once.
you do not have to teach the whole song at once. you could begin with a short part, sing it slowly, and let her try before moving on.
i do not want her to feel wrong if she cannot remember a word.
you can keep the first goal small and say that it is okay not to remember everything at first. you could sing the line again together rather than stop every time something is not right.
what could i say if she says she forgot a word?
you could say: that is okay. we can sing the line again together. you do not have to remember everything at once.
give me something i could say before we start.
we can do this slowly. let us try one line together, and we can go back if you need to hear it again.
what if she wants to sing the whole song before learning each part?
you can ask which way helps her more. hearing the whole song first may help her understand how the parts go together.
use only the words we have for that last sentence.
she may want to hear the whole song first so she knows how the short parts go together.
my father told my brother that his book was on the table. whose book was on the table?
the sentence does not make that clear by itself. his could be about your father or your brother.
i mean the book is for my brother. my father was just telling him where it was.
then you could say: my father told my brother that the book on the table was for my brother.
could i say my brother left it there if i did not tell you that?
no. you told me where the book was, but not who left it there. saying your brother left it would add a new fact.
can you make the sentence about my father shorter?
my father told my brother where the book was.
does that still tell us whose book it was?
no. the short sentence leaves that part out. to keep it clear, say: my father told my brother that the book on the table was for my brother.
can using my brother again be useful even if it makes the sentence longer?
yes. using my brother again can keep the meaning clear when a word like his could be about more than one person.
use only our words and give just the clear sentence.
my father told my brother that the book on the table was for my brother.
what is the difference between i read the book yesterday and i have been reading the book?
the first sentence puts the reading on yesterday. the other says reading the book has been part of what you have been doing, without saying that yesterday was the only time.
does have been reading mean i finished the whole book?
no. it does not by itself say the book is finished. you could still be reading it.
can i say i have been reading it for a week, but i am not finished yet?
yes. that makes clear both how long you have been reading and that the book is not finished yet.
make that explanation shorter.
yes. you have said how long you have been reading and that you have not finished the book.
what if i say i read it yesterday and finished it last night?
then you are saying the whole book was finished last night. that gives more information than i read the book yesterday alone.
i want one sentence about starting last week and still reading now.
i started reading the book last week, and i am still reading it now.
can a small change in time words change what we know?
yes. the time words can tell us when something happened and whether it is still happening.
if i say i knew the answer last week, does that mean i know it now?
not always. you could remember it now, or you could no longer know it. the sentence only gives us information about last week.
give me an explanation with the word forgot in it.
you might still know the answer now. but it is also possible to say i knew it last week, but i forgot it.
give me only the example sentence.
i knew it last week, but i forgot it.
what if i say i knew it last week and still know it now?
then you have made the part about now clear too.
give me an example of knowing a place rather than an answer.
i knew where the library was last year, and i still know where it is now.
what if the library moved to a different building?
then knowing the old place would not be enough to know the new place. you would need the new information.
write a sentence that keeps what i knew before apart from what i know now.
i knew where the library was before it moved, but i do not know where it is now.
my sister and i both chose to stay home. she wanted to read, and i wanted to rest. does choosing the same thing mean we wanted the same thing?
you chose the same place to spend time, but you gave different reasons. she wanted reading time, and you wanted rest.
what if our cousin says we must both hate going out?
that would add a reason you did not give. choosing to stay home today does not show that either of you always feels hate for going out.
make that answer shorter.
you have not said you never enjoy going out. you only told me why you chose home today.
can i say we wanted different things from the same afternoon?
yes. that keeps clear both your plan to stay home and your different reasons.
give me a more simple answer about what we wanted.
yes. you both stayed home, but you wanted rest and she wanted time to read.
what if i ask you which reason was better?
i would need to know what each person needs that afternoon. there is no need to make one reason wrong just because the reasons are different.
keep it simple and give me a short answer.
both reasons can be good for the person who has them.
my little sister keeps taking my book while i am reading. i want a short sentence about when she can use it.
i am reading it now. you can have a turn when i finish.
what if i do not know when i will finish?
you can say she needs to wait and that you will tell her when the book is free. do not give her a specific time if you do not know it.
give me just the sentence to tell her.
you can say: i am using the book now. i will tell you when you can have a turn.
should i say i will never finish so she stops asking?
not if that is not true. it could also make her think she will never have a turn. a clear answer about now is enough.
i do want her to read it later. write a kind answer that says both things.
i want you to have a turn too. i am reading now, and i will tell you when i finish.
why does too help there?
it makes clear that you also want her to get a turn, even though she cannot take the book right now.
give me a shorter explanation of too in that sentence.
it makes clear that you want her to have a turn as well.
make this sentence better: i saw my friend with a camera.
do you mean you had the camera, or your friend had it? the sentence can be read either way.
my friend had it. i did not have a camera.
then you could say: i saw my friend holding a camera.
what if i only know it was with him, not that it was in his hand?
then holding would add something you do not know. you could say: my friend had a camera with him when i saw him.
now make it shorter.
my friend had a camera when i saw him.
does that mean the camera is his own?
not by itself. he could have been using a camera that is for someone else to keep.
say that in a shorter way.
not by itself. the camera could be for someone else to keep, while your friend was using it then.
why did you ask a question before changing my first sentence?
because the first sentence could mean different things. knowing which meaning you wanted helped keep the new sentence true to your idea.
write a story about someone waiting until a friend is ready. keep it about a simple visit.

a man came to see his friend in the afternoon. she was still finishing a letter at the kitchen table. he asked whether he should come back later. she said she only needed a few more minutes and asked him to sit by the window. he looked at the garden and waited until she put the letter away. then they made tea and talked about their week. he was happy he had asked instead of starting a long conversation while she was trying to finish.
tell me what until does in the story.
until makes the end of the wait clear. he waited while she finished the letter, and the next part began when she put it away.
did he have to leave after she put it away?
no. putting the letter away was the end of the wait, not the end of the visit. after that, they made tea and talked.
say that in a different way.
putting the letter away was the end of the wait, not the end of the visit. they stayed together for tea and conversation.
can you say he waited until she began the letter?
that would change the story. she was finishing the letter, and he waited for her to put it away.
what is the opposite of open? just the word.
closed
now put both words in one sentence about a door.
the door was open before, but it is closed now.
make the sentence about a window instead.
the window was open before, but it is closed now.
what did i change in that request?
you changed the object from a door to a window. the words open and closed stayed in the sentence.
can you write a whole story about why it closed?
i can write an example story, but your sentence does not give a real reason for a real window closing.
i do not want a story after all. just give me the sentence about the window again.
the window was open before, but it is closed now.
why did you not add how it happened?
because you asked for just the sentence. adding a reason would give you something you did not ask for.
give me a shorter explanation of why you kept it short.
you asked me to give the sentence again. you did not ask me to add a reason.
my aunt sent a message saying the visit is tomorrow. my uncle sent one saying it is today. i do not know which one is right.
those messages give different days. before making a plan around either one, you could ask them to check the day together and tell you the same answer.
should i choose my aunt answer just because hers came first?
not from that alone. the first message could be right or could have been changed later. you need to know which day is now the plan.
say that in a shorter way.
you need to ask which day they now want for the visit. the order of the messages by itself is not enough.
write one message to both of them.
i have one message saying today and another saying tomorrow. could you please tell me which day the visit will be?
my aunt answers that they changed it to today after she sent the first message.
then you have a clear explanation for the difference. the new plan is today, and her first message was about the plan before it changed.
give me only the day.
today.
i remember a holiday with my family as a good time, but i do not want to go to the same place again. is that wrong?
not from what you said. you can have a good memory of one holiday and still want the next trip to be different. what did you enjoy most about that holiday?
use only the words we have. i liked being with my family, but the journey was too long for me.
then you can keep the good part as family time and choose a place with a shorter journey next time.
my brother says that choosing a new place must mean i did not enjoy the holiday.
that does not follow from what you said. you enjoyed being with your family and found the journey hard. both can be true.
write a reply to him that keeps those two things clear.
i enjoyed our time together. i would like another family visit, but i want a place with a shorter journey this time.
should i say the old place was very wrong for us just to make my point?
that would say more than you told me. a clear reply can explain the change you want without saying the whole holiday was wrong.
use only simple words and give me a short last answer.
you can ask for a shorter journey without giving up the good memory of being together.
